title: Arms Sales Notification
items_summary: Aircraft ferry support and other related logistics and program support added to a previously implemented FMS case (JA-D-QFB) that originally included AN/ARC-210 radios, high frequency radios, modifications, communications equipment, spares, software, publications, and engineering/logistics support.
summary: The Government of Japan has requested an amendment to Foreign Military Sales case JA-D-QFB (originally valued at $99.9 million, below the notification threshold) to add aircraft ferry support and related logistics and program support, bringing the total estimated value to $159 million with no Major Defense Equipment. The amendment pushes the case over the congressional notification threshold, so the full program is notified; the policy justification states it will improve Japan's ISR and airborne early warning and control capabilities and strengthen a major Pacific ally. The notice also includes sensitivity-of-technology annex covering AN/ARC-210 secure communications (SECRET level). Only one transmittal (26-91) is included in this notice.

DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE

Office of the Secretary

[Transmittal No. 26-91]


Arms Sales Notification

AGENCY: Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Department of 
Defense (DoD).

ACTION: Arms sales notice.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The DoD (referred to herein as ``the Department,'' 
``Department of War'' or ``DoW'') is publishing the unclassified text 
of an arms sales notification.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Urooj Zahra at (703) 695-6233, 
[email protected], or [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 36(b) arms sales notification is 
published to fulfill the requirements of section 155 of

[[Page 75309]]

Public Law 104-164 dated July 21, 1996. The following is a copy of the 
attached Transmittal 26-91, Policy Justification, and Sensitivity of 
Technology.

    Dated: November 17, 2026.
Stephanie J. Bost,
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.
Transmittal No. 26-91
Notice of Proposed Issuance of Letter of Offer Pursuant to Section 
36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act, as amended
    (i) Prospective Purchaser: Government of Japan
    (ii) Total Estimated Value:

Major Defense Equipment *...............  $ 0
Other...................................  $159 million
                                         -------------------------------
  TOTAL.................................  $159 million
 

    (iii) Description and Quantity or Quantities of Articles or 
Services under Consideration for Purchase: Foreign Military Sales case 
JA-D-QFB was below congressional notification threshold at $99.9 
million ($0 in MDE) and included AN/ARC-210 radios; high frequency 
radios; major and minor modifications support and equipment; 
communications equipment; spare parts, consumables and accessories, and 
repair and return support; classified and unclassified software 
delivery and support; classified and unclassified publications and 
technical documentation; transportation support; and U.S. Government 
and contractor engineering, technical, and logistics support services. 
The Government of Japan has requested the case be amended to include 
aircraft ferry support; and other related elements of logistics and 
program support. This amendment will cause the case to exceed the 
notification threshold, and thus notification of the entire program is 
required. The above notification requirements are combined as follows:

Major Defense Equipment (MDE):
    None
Non-MDE:
    The following non-MDE items will be included: aircraft ferry 
support; AN/ARC-210 radios; high frequency radios; major and minor 
modifications support and equipment; communications equipment; spare 
parts, consumables and accessories; and repair and return support; 
classified and unclassified software delivery and support; classified 
and unclassified publications and technical documentation; 
transportation support; and U.S. Government and contractor engineering, 
technical, and logistics support services; and other related elements 
of logistics and program support.

    (iv) Military Department: Air Force (JA-D-QFB)
    (v) Prior Related Cases, if any: None
    (vi) Sales Commission, Fee, etc., Paid, Offered, or Agreed to be 
Paid: None known at this time
    (vii) Sensitivity of Technology Contained in the Defense Article or 
Defense Services Proposed to be Sold: See Attached Annex
    (viii) Date Report Delivered to Congress: September 22, 2026
    * as defined in Section 47(6) of the Arms Export Control Act.

POLICY JUSTIFICATION

Japan--Ferry Support

    The Government of Japan has requested to buy aircraft ferry 
support; and other related elements of logistics and program support 
that will be added to a previously implemented case whose value was 
under the congressional notification threshold. The original Foreign 
Military Sales case, valued at $99.9 million ($0 in MDE), included AN/
ARC-210 radios; high frequency radios; major and minor modifications 
support and equipment; communications equipment; spare parts, 
consumables and accessories; and repair and return support; classified 
and unclassified software delivery and support; classified and 
unclassified publications and technical documentation; transportation 
support; and U.S. Government and contractor engineering, technical, and 
logistics support services; and other related elements of logistics and 
program support. The estimated total cost is $159 million.
    This proposed sale will enhance the foreign policy and national 
security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a 
major ally that is a force for political stability and economic 
progress in the Pacific region.
    The proposed sale will improve Japan's capability to meet current 
and future threats by providing increased intelligence, surveillance, 
and reconnaissance, and airborne early warning and control 
capabilities. Japan will have no difficulty absorbing these articles 
and services into its armed forces.
    The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the 
basic military balance in the region.
    The principal contractor will be The Boeing Company, located in 
Arlington, VA. At this time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any 
offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any 
offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser 
and the contractor.
    Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the 
assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor 
representatives to Japan.
    There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a 
result of this proposed sale.
Transmittal No. 26-91
Notice of Proposed Issuance of Letter of Offer Pursuant to Section 
36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act
Annex
Item No. vii
    (vii) Sensitivity of Technology:
    1. The AN/ARC-210 provides secure, jam-resistant, line-of-sight and 
satellite communications, and is configured with HAVE QUICK II and 
Second-Generation Anti-jam Tactical Ultra High Frequency Radio for NATO 
(SATURN), which enables survival and communication in highly contested 
electronic warfare environments. Both waveforms rely directly on Type 1 
Cryptography to encrypt tactical voice and data traffic and securing 
the radio's frequency-hopping pattern. Other waveforms may be included 
as needed.
    2. The highest level of classification of defense articles, 
components, and services included in this potential sale is SECRET.
    3. If a technologically advanced adversary were to obtain knowledge 
of the specific hardware and software elements, the information could 
be used to develop countermeasures that might reduce system 
effectiveness or be used in the development of a system with similar or 
advanced capabilities.
    4. A determination has been made that Japan can provide 
substantially the same degree of protection for the sensitive 
technology being released as the U.S. Government. This proposed sale is 
necessary in furtherance of the U.S. foreign policy and national 
security objectives outlined in the Policy Justification.
    5. All defense articles and services listed in this transmittal 
have been authorized for release and export to the Government of Japan.
